paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi had his sights set on the capital; with everyone else, a judicious blend of intimidation and conciliation would suffice. He adopted two measures: the first was to simplify military discipline and encourage his men to win distinction; the second was to punish wrongdoing. Then, without pausing for breath, he headed straight for Kiyosu Castle.

paragraphs.source_en: Shibata Katsuie, too, concluded the fighting in Hokuriku on the twenty-sixth and hurried to Kiyosu Castle. Niwa Nagahide had already arrived at Kiyosu with Nobutaka, and Ikeda Nobuteru entered the castle after Hideyoshi. Once Takigawa Kazumasu arrived, all the Oda clan's senior retainers and veteran commanders would be assembled. Unfortunately, on his return march Kazumasu had been challenged by Hōjō Ujinao at the Kanna River in Musashi and had therefore not yet returned.

paragraphs.source_en: At the proposal of the senior retainer Katsuie, a great council concerning the succession to the headship and the division of Nobunaga's former domains was convened in the main hall of Kiyosu Castle at about the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Snake on the morning of the twenty-seventh.
